t: You are standing where Bridewell Palace once stood, in the City of London. It was built as a residence for Henry VIII, and he lived here for eight years early in his reign. His son, Edward VI, gave it to the City in 1553, and it became Bridewell Hospital, an orphanage and a place of correction for wayward women. Later it became the first prison and poorhouse to have an appointed doctor. Joan Larke, mistress of Thomas Wolsey and mother of his two illegitimate children, lived here. Elizeus Hall, who claimed to be a messenger from God, died here.
